synopsis: Cadence completed its acquisition of Hexagon’s Design & Engineering business, including Virtual Test Drive (VTD), on 23 February 2026; the glossary records the transfer of VTD and VTDx ownership in February 2026 [f8330, f8432, f8880, f15891]. Cadence’s reported total consideration was USD 3,101,008 thousand, consistent with the approximately USD 3.1 billion summary, while Hexagon cited approximately EUR 2.7 billion in cash and Cadence stock; the acquired business contributed about EUR 265 million of 2024 revenue [f8883, f8330, f8881, f8882]. The tools chapter includes VTD and VTDx among complete or near-complete simulation platforms and describes VTD as a long-standing commercial on-road ADAS platform covering road networks, scenarios, vehicle dynamics, traffic, sensor perception, SIL, DIL and HIL [f8347, f8426]. However, the glossary characterizes the available evidence for both platforms as on-road-only and reports that public prices were not found, leaving off-road suitability and pricing unresolved in these facts [f15890]. Cadence’s notices list VTD 2026.2, but the ownership change is explicitly identified as a lifecycle and roadmap transition risk [f8431, f8435].
